The Hartwell Family | Serving in Northern Uganda
November 2026 Update

Dear Friends and Partners,

Greetings from Gulu! It has been a full season, and we are sorry it has been four months since our last letter. Grab a cup of coffee, because there is a lot to share.

--- A FLOOD, A FALLEN ROOF, AND A FAMILY WE DID NOT EXPECT ---

In mid-September the rains came early and hard. Over one weekend the river behind our neighborhood rose about six feet. On Saturday night, our neighbor Mama Grace* (a widow who sells vegetables at the market and raises four grandchildren) knocked on our gate at 2 a.m. Her mud-brick house had started to collapse. By morning the back wall was gone and the roof had caved in over the children's sleeping room. Nobody was hurt, thank God, but they lost nearly everything: mattresses, school uniforms, her cooking pots, and the little stock she keeps for her stall.

For two weeks, all five of them slept in our living room. Our kids gave up their bunk beds. It was loud, crowded, and one of the sweetest things we have done as a family. Mama Grace told Emily one night, "I have gone to church all my life, but I never saw it with my own eyes until now." We did not preach a word. We just made rice and beans and kept the door open.

The house is still not rebuilt. A local builder quoted us 6,800,000 Ugandan shillings (about $1,850) for a new roof, two walls, and a cement floor that will not wash out again. Our partnership team has set aside some money, but we are still short. See the one-time needs section below.

--- LANGUAGE SCHOOL AND A SURPRISE AT CHURCH ---

Meanwhile, Luke has continued Acholi language lessons three mornings a week. Last month he gave his first five-minute devotional in Acholi at Pastor Moses's church. He mispronounced one word and accidentally told the congregation that "God is a goat." They laughed kindly, and Pastor Moses has been teasing him about it ever since. Slow progress, but real progress.

On the ministry side, the youth Bible study that began with six teenagers in June now regularly has twenty-two. Several of them are former child soldiers' children or kids who have been out of school for years. One of them, a sixteen-year-old named Denis*, asked Luke last week whether God could forgive his father, who is in prison. Luke did not have a quick answer. He has been thinking about it ever since and is meeting Denis again Tuesday. It was a good reminder that the Spirit is far ahead of us.

--- A HARD MONTH FOR OUR TEAM ---

In October, our teammate Joseph* (the Ugandan pastor who has partnered with us since the beginning) lost his mother after a short illness. We traveled six hours by road to attend the burial in his home village. The roads were terrible and our truck's rear axle started making a grinding noise on the way home. The mechanic in Gulu says the axle and a worn differential must be replaced before we can safely drive on the rural roads again. This matters because our youth Bible study students and two village churches are only reachable by truck. The quote is 4,200,000 shillings, about $1,150. We have been borrowing a motorbike from Pastor Moses in the meantime, which is fine for one person and not great in the rain.

Joseph has returned to work but he is clearly grieving. He told Luke he feels guilty that he was away from his mother during her last months because of ministry travel. We are walking closely with him.

--- AN UNEXPECTED OPENING WITH THE DISTRICT SCHOOLS ---

Also in October, the district education office called Emily. Out of nowhere, an official asked whether our team would be willing to offer a weekly "life skills and character" class in four public primary schools. Government schools here do not normally allow outside faith groups, and she was told they heard about our work from parents. The pilot would begin in January if our paperwork is approved. We submitted the application on October 28. The official said a decision could take four to eight weeks. We do not know whether this is a door that will open or quietly close, and we are trying to hold it loosely. Emily has been drafting a curriculum with Joseph, built around stories of Jesus's character without being overtly sermon-like, at least to start.

--- A QUICK PRAISE REPORT ---

We want to thank you for praying for Sophie's health last spring. Our youngest had malaria twice this year, and she has been healthy and strong for the last three months. We are also grateful that our residence permit renewal came through in August, a full month early. God is kind.

--- THE FUNDING NEEDS ---

We rarely write about money in these letters, but a few one-time needs have come up at once, and we want to be open with you.

1. Mama Grace's house: We are trying to raise the remaining $1,100 so the builder can begin before the heavy rains return in March. Gifts of any size toward this are appreciated. We will send photos as work progresses.

2. Truck repair: The $1,150 axle and differential repair is needed as soon as possible. We would love to have it done before the end of November. Any amount helps. Any gifts beyond what is needed for the repair will go toward our regular vehicle maintenance fund.

3. Team retreat: Our regional team gathers each January for a three-day retreat for rest, prayer, and planning. Registration is $420 per family and is due by December 5. We usually pay this from our own budget, but the flood and the truck have stretched us this year. This one is optional, but it matters to us. We are nearly worn out and need it.

Please do not feel any pressure. If you have already given generously this year, thank you. Your faithfulness is why we are here at all.

--- HOW YOU CAN PRAY ---

We would be so grateful if you would pray with us for the following.

First, please pray for Mama Grace and her grandchildren. They are still in a rented single room across town while their house is rebuilt, and the youngest, Peace*, has been coughing for two weeks. Pray that they stay healthy and that the rebuild goes smoothly. Pray too that Mama Grace's heart stays open to Jesus.

Please also keep Joseph in your prayers as he grieves, and pray for his wife and three young children as they care for him. Pray that he finds rest and that the guilt he is carrying would lift.

Pray for the district schools application. Pray for wisdom for the officials and that, if it is from the Lord, it would be approved before the end of the year. If not, pray that we respond with grace.

Please pray for Denis, the teenager we mentioned, and for his father. Pray that Denis would find peace and that Luke would have wisdom in how to answer his questions.

Finally, please pray for our family's rest. Between the flood, the guests, and the truck trouble, we are tired. Pray that the retreat in January would be a real refreshment for us, and for the kids that they continue to adjust well to school here.

Every month we are reminded that the work here is God's, not ours. Thank you for being part of it with us.

With gratitude,
Luke, Emily, Noah, Ruth, and Sophie Hartwell

*Names changed for security.
